almost-01.invariant: 存在一个可辨识的达成阈值，实际状态沿某维度逼近到极近处，但最终未跨越阈值。
l1_confusables: 中文"几乎"也覆盖 nearly/practically；中文"几乎不"表达 hardly/barely， 学习者容易把 almost not 直译。
中文"差点"偏向未发生的负面事件并带庆幸语气，almost 无此限制。

dirty-01.invariant: 对象表面附着了一种不受欢迎的外来物质，使表面偏离其应有的洁净基线；该偏离 可被直接感知。判断对象是表面状态，不是位置的秩序。
l1_confusables: 中文"脏乱"常连用，使学习者把 dirty（表面附着）与 messy（位置无序）绑定成 一个概念，需要分别验证两条维度。
中文"脏"同时覆盖物理不洁与言语粗俗（dirty-02），物理表面义项须与引申义分开。

messy-01.invariant: 一个可被整体观察的空间或对象，其组成部分偏离了预期/常规的排列与形态，形成 整体可见的无序；判断对象是位置与排列秩序，不是表面附着。
l1_confusables: 中文"乱"覆盖物理空间、抽象局面与行为秩序；messy 在日常英语中主要指可见的 物理无序，需要把"乱"的经验范围收窄到可观察的排列。
中文"脏乱"连用使学习者把 messy 与 dirty 绑定，需要分别验证两条维度。

reluctant-01.invariant: 面对一个可执行行动或行动方案时，主观意愿为负（unwillingness / inner resistance）；行为上必须有可观察证据支持该负意愿，但任何单一行为都不是定义条件。
l1_confusables: 中文"不情愿"常同时覆盖 reluctant 与 unwilling；学习者容易忽略 reluctant 的 "可能仍会做"的一面，把"不愿做"与"拒绝做"混为一谈。
中文"犹豫"覆盖 hesitant，学习者容易把"拿不定主意"当成"不想做"。

semantic_model.invariant: 存在一个可辨识的达成阈值，实际状态沿某维度逼近到极近处，但最终未跨越阈值。
l1_interference: 中文"几乎"也覆盖 nearly/practically；中文"几乎不"表达 hardly/barely， 学习者容易把 almost not 直译。
中文"差点"偏向未发生的负面事件并带庆幸语气，almost 无此限制。

misconceptions.correction: almost 的核心是"未达成"本身；事件没有发生。判定要看结果是否停在阈值外， 而不是看接近的过程。
misconceptions.description: almost 意味着事件最终还是发生了（把 almost fell 当成 fell）。

misconceptions.correction: about 表示近似相等，不强调差距大小；almost 必须距离阈值极小。距离还远 时是 not yet / approaching，不是 almost。
misconceptions.description: 只要"大约/大概"接近就可以说 almost，不需要极度接近。

misconceptions.correction: 一旦跨越阈值就是达成（barely），almost 要求结果停在阈值之外；未达成本身 才是 almost 的成立条件。
misconceptions.description: 刚好越过阈值也叫 almost（把勉强达成与未达成混淆）。

necessary_conditions: 存在明确可辨识的达成阈值（终点、满、到达、完成等）。

non_entailments: 极度接近不蕴涵达成（阈值未被跨越）。

typical_correlates: 观众产生"就要到达/就要发生"的预期。
距离、数量、时间或程度上只差一小截。

semantic_model.invariant: 一个可被整体观察的空间或对象，其组成部分偏离了预期/常规的排列与形态，形成 整体可见的无序；判断对象是位置与排列秩序，不是表面附着。
l1_interference: 中文"乱"覆盖物理空间、抽象局面与行为秩序；messy 在日常英语中主要指可见的 物理无序，需要把"乱"的经验范围收窄到可观察的排列。
中文"脏乱"连用使学习者把 messy 与 dirty 绑定，需要分别验证两条维度。

misconceptions.correction: messy 判断位置与排列秩序，dirty 判断表面是否有污物；两条维度独立。 固定表面状态、只改变位置秩序，看目标词是否成立。
misconceptions.description: 乱 = 脏（把 messy 与 dirty 混为一体）。

misconceptions.correction: 乱的定义是"偏离预期排列"，与数量无关；少量物品只要位置全错，同样成立。
misconceptions.description: 只有物品很多、堆得满满当当才算乱。

necessary_conditions: 存在一个可被整体观察的空间、对象或可见产物。
整体由多个物品、部分或可见细节构成。
这些组成部分偏离其常规、预期或整齐的排列与形态。
无序达到整体可见的程度。
non_entailments: 排列无序不蕴涵表面附着污物。
表面附着污物不蕴涵排列无序。
排列无序不蕴涵物品数量多（少量物品错位同样成立）。
排列无序不蕴涵蓄意破坏。
typical_correlates: 相同类型物品分散在不同位置。
物品方向不一致、相互交叠。
与同一空间的整洁对照状态形成对比。

reveal.presentation: Return to the desk scene. The word "messy" names the state of that desk: parts out of their expected places, readable at a glance — separate from any marks on their surfaces.

experience.episode: A study desk after homework: the notebook lies open at a slant on top of the keyboard, three pencils rest among the keys, a cup sits upside down beside the lamp, and the pages of the book stick out at different angles.
observable_evidence: The notebook lies at a slant on top of the keyboard instead of its usual spot.
Three pencils rest among the keyboard keys.
The cup sits upside down beside the lamp.
The book's pages stick out at different angles.

surface_dimensions.baseline: each item in its usual place
surface_dimensions.deviation: notebook on the keyboard, pencils in the keys, cup upside down
surface_dimensions.name: placement

surface_dimensions.deviation: slanted notebook, pages at different angles
surface_dimensions.name: orientation

answers.feedback: The number of items is small, but every one of them sits where it does not belong. Disorder is about placement, not about how many things there are.
answers.text: Yes — the few items are all out of their usual places, which reads as disorder.

answers.feedback: Quantity is not part of the meaning. A few misplaced items with no order between them is still a visible disorder.
answers.text: No — with so few items, it cannot be called that.

interaction.question: Only a few items sit on this desk. Is the desk described by the target meaning?

semantic_spec.arrangement_baseline: each item in its usual place
semantic_spec.judgment: 少量物品位置全错，是否构成整体可见的无序？

experience.episode: A playroom at the end of the day: a building-block tower lies collapsed in the middle of the rug, toy cars sit on the bookshelf, a teddy bear hangs upside down from the window curtain, and puzzle pieces cover the floor in small scattered piles.
observable_evidence: The block tower lies collapsed on the rug.
Toy cars sit on the bookshelf where no car belongs.
The teddy bear hangs upside down from the curtain.
Puzzle pieces scatter across the floor in small piles.

surface_dimensions.baseline: toys kept in the toy box
surface_dimensions.deviation: cars on the shelf, bear on the curtain, blocks on the rug
surface_dimensions.name: placement

surface_dimensions.deviation: puzzle pieces spread across the floor in piles
surface_dimensions.name: scatter

answers.feedback: Every kind of toy sits somewhere unexpected, and the pieces spread out without order. The room visibly departs from its usual arrangement.
answers.text: The toys are out of their expected places, so the room reads as jumbled.

answers.feedback: Being in the room is not the same as being in the right place. The meaning is about the arrangement of things, not about whether they are present at all.
answers.text: The toys are still in the room, so nothing changed.

interaction.question: The room is full of toys in the wrong places. Which statement fits best?

semantic_spec.arrangement_baseline: toys kept in the toy box
semantic_spec.judgment: 换到更大的空间与更多物品，无序是否仍然成立？

experience.episode: A kitchen counter with just three things: a sponge lying on the chopping board, a knife resting on the counter beside the cutting area, and a plate sitting on top of the dish rack instead of inside it. Each item looks new and carries no marks or stains.
observable_evidence: The sponge lies on the chopping board instead of its holder.
The knife rests on the counter next to the cutting area.
The plate sits on top of the dish rack instead of inside it.
Every item looks new, with no marks on it.

surface_dimensions.deviation: all three items sit somewhere unexpected
surface_dimensions.name: placement

surface_dimensions.deviation: surfaces stay unmarked while placement is wrong
surface_dimensions.name: surface_condition

answers.feedback: The surfaces carry nothing, yet the arrangement is wrong on all three items. This shows the meaning lives in placement; surface marks are a separate thing.
answers.text: The counter is jumbled because the placement is wrong, not because of any marks.

answers.feedback: Marks are about the surface, not about arrangement. A counter with clean items that all sit in the wrong places is still a disorder of placement.
answers.text: Without any marks, nothing can be wrong with the counter.

interaction.question: The three items are all spotless, but none of them is in its place. Which description fits best?

semantic_spec.judgment: 每件物品都干净无痕时，位置错位是否仍然成立？

experience.episode: A child wakes up after a restless sleep. Her hair sticks out in several directions: a tuft stands up at the crown, a strand lies across her cheek, and the back is flattened on one side while the other side springs outward. There is no single smooth line from front to back.
observable_evidence: A tuft of hair stands up at the crown.
A strand lies across the cheek.
The back of the hair flattens on one side and springs out on the other.
No part of the hair follows a single smooth line.

surface_dimensions.deviation: strands point in several directions
surface_dimensions.name: orientation

surface_dimensions.baseline: smooth silhouette from front to back
surface_dimensions.deviation: uneven silhouette with tufts and flattened sides
surface_dimensions.name: contour

answers.feedback: Hair is made of many small strands, and here they point in different directions with an uneven outline. The meaning transfers from rooms to hair because the structure is the same: parts out of their expected arrangement.
answers.text: The hair is jumbled because its strands and shape left the expected arrangement.

answers.feedback: The meaning is about any visible whole made of parts; a head of hair is exactly that. The domain changes, the judgment does not.
answers.text: Hair cannot be described by this meaning because it is not a room.

interaction.question: The child's hair has no marks on it, only disorder. Which statement fits best?

semantic_spec.arrangement_baseline: hair combed into a smooth shape
semantic_spec.judgment: 从房间换到头发，无序是否仍然成立？

grounding.l2_realization: Leo was reluctant to eat his greens.

dimensions.name: semantic_correctness
dimensions.note: 全部正例落在"面对可执行行动时主观意愿为负"的 invariant 内。

dimensions.name: sense_purity
dimensions.note: eventual_action yes/no 双值、无外部压力、无行动三种结果均保持词义成立，未滑向 refuse/unwilling。

dimensions.name: prototype_quality
dimensions.note: anchor 是最典型的"愿意负但做了"实例，行为证据充分。

dimensions.name: definition_leakage
dimensions.note: 语义全部由行为承载，无旁白式定义。

dimensions.name: l2_leakage
dimensions.note: 揭示前内容无目标词与相邻词。

dimensions.name: variable_isolation
dimensions.note: 每个单元单变量或少数受控变量变化，其余保持。

dimensions.name: accidental_invariant
dimensions.note: eventual_action 在正例间显式变化，没有假不变式。

dimensions.name: transfer_novelty
dimensions.note: transfer 换到成年人办公场景，改变四个表面维度。

dimensions.name: cognitive_noise
dimensions.note: 叙事短、动作单一，无无关认知负担。

experience.episode: A new gym member walks onto the floor for the first time. She stands in front of a treadmill for a long time, reties her shoelaces twice, then finally steps on and starts walking slowly.
observable_evidence: She stands in front of the treadmill without stepping on.
She reties her shoelaces a second time.
She steps on in the end and walks slowly.

surface_dimensions.baseline: steps on the treadmill at once
surface_dimensions.deviation: stands still, then ties her shoes again
surface_dimensions.name: start_delay

surface_dimensions.deviation: starts slowly in the end
surface_dimensions.name: outcome

semantic_spec.judgment: 换到健身房场景，负意愿 + 最终行动是否仍然成立？

experience.episode: After washing the dishes, a man picks up a plate from the rack, looks at the cupboard, holds the plate for a moment, then puts it back on the counter, turns around, and leaves the kitchen. The plate stays on the counter.
observable_evidence: He picks the plate up but does not open the cupboard.
He holds the plate for a moment, then sets it back down.
He leaves the plate on the counter and walks away.

surface_dimensions.baseline: opens the cupboard and puts the plate away
surface_dimensions.deviation: picks the plate up, then puts it back on the counter
surface_dimensions.name: approach

surface_dimensions.deviation: plate stays on the counter
surface_dimensions.name: outcome

semantic_spec.judgment: 负意愿 + 最终没有行动，在厨房场景是否仍然成立？

semantic_model.invariant: 面对一个可执行行动或行动方案时，主观意愿为负（unwillingness / inner resistance）；行为上必须有可观察证据支持该负意愿，但任何单一行为都不是定义条件。
l1_interference: 中文"不情愿"常同时覆盖 reluctant 与 unwilling；学习者容易忽略 reluctant 的 "可能仍会做"的一面，把"不愿做"与"拒绝做"混为一谈。
中文"犹豫"覆盖 hesitant，学习者容易把"拿不定主意"当成"不想做"。

misconceptions.correction: 即使最终完成了行动，只要在行动过程中负意愿清晰可观察（慢、叹气、皱眉）， 仍然是 reluctant；eventual_action=yes 与 =no 都兼容。
misconceptions.description: 只有"最终没做"才叫不情愿；做了就不算。

misconceptions.correction: 只要拒绝之外有独立的负意愿行为证据（转身、停顿、叹气），最终没做同样支持 reluctant；只有 bare refusal 本身不足够。
misconceptions.description: 最终没做 + 拒绝 = 一定不是 reluctant（把 no-action 结果与 refuse 绑定）。

misconceptions.correction: 面对任何可执行行动，即使没有任何人要求或监督，内心的负意愿同样成立。
misconceptions.description: 必须有外部压力（别人要求、命令）才算 reluctant。

misconceptions.correction: 积极的犹豫（愿意但不确定选哪个）不是 reluctant；reluctant 是已经确定的 负意愿，两者要在同一判断任务中区分。
misconceptions.description: 犹豫（在两个选项间权衡）就等于不想做。

necessary_conditions: 体验者正面对一个可执行行动或行动方案。
体验者对该行动的主观意愿为负（内在抵触或不愿意）。
负意愿由可观察行为支持，但不要求任何特定行为（叹气、拖延、表情、拒绝等都不是必要条件）。
行动最终是否发生不影响词义：做与不做都成立。
non_entailments: 最终没有行动不蕴涵"不是 reluctant"（"最终没做"绝不能被排除）。
拒绝了（bare refusal）不蕴涵 reluctant——拒绝本身不足够，需要额外的负意愿行为证据。
最终完成了行动不蕴涵"不是 reluctant"。
外部压力存在与否不蕴涵 reluctant——没有外部压力也可以 reluctant。
叹气、拖延、皱眉等任何单一现象都不蕴涵 reluctant。
typical_correlates: 行动前有明显的启动延迟或反复试探。
叹气、撇嘴、眉头紧皱等面部信号。
身体回避：转身、后退、身体远离行动对象。
若行动发生，动作变慢、幅度变小、接触时间变短。

reveal.presentation: Return to the dinner scene. The word "reluctant" names the state Leo was in: an available action, an inner "I do not want to do this", and a body that shows it — whether he finally does the action or not.

experience.episode: At dinner, Leo's mother sets a bowl of boiled greens in front of him. He stares at the bowl, picks up his fork, then puts it down again. He lets out a long sigh, turns his head away, and finally lifts a single small piece to his mouth, chewing it very slowly with his brows pressed together.
observable_evidence: He picks up the fork, then puts it down before starting.
A long audible sigh before he eats anything.
He turns his head away from the bowl while still eating.
He chews the single piece very slowly with his brows pressed together.

surface_dimensions.baseline: reaches for the food without pausing
surface_dimensions.deviation: starts and stops, then moves very slowly
surface_dimensions.name: approach_speed

surface_dimensions.deviation: turns the head away while still complying
surface_dimensions.name: body_orientation

surface_dimensions.deviation: a long audible sigh before starting
surface_dimensions.name: vocal_evidence

answers.feedback: His pauses, his sigh, and his turned-away head are signs that he did not want to do it; he still ate a little, which is allowed — doing it does not erase the inner resistance.
answers.text: He did not want to eat them, and his body showed it while he still ate a little.

answers.feedback: A hungry, happy eater would not pause, sigh, and turn away; his behavior pointed the other way.
answers.text: He was hungry and enjoyed the food.

interaction.question: What did Leo's behavior show about how he felt about eating the greens?

semantic_spec.judgment: 主角对眼前可做的行动意愿如何？

experience.episode: At noon, a colleague waves to Mira and calls her name for the team lunch. Mira walks to the door, grabs the door frame with her fingers, takes a slow deep breath, then turns around and walks back to her desk. She does not join the lunch.
observable_evidence: She walks toward the door but stops there.
Her fingers grip the door frame instead of opening the door.
A slow deep breath before she turns around.
She walks back to her desk and stays there.

surface_dimensions.deviation: stops at the door and never crosses it
surface_dimensions.name: approach_distance

surface_dimensions.baseline: opens the door with a smooth reach
surface_dimensions.deviation: grips the door frame and pauses
surface_dimensions.name: grip_behavior

surface_dimensions.deviation: returns to the desk, no action
surface_dimensions.name: outcome

answers.feedback: She was not pushed, and she never said no out loud; her grip on the door frame and her breath before turning back are the readable signs. The fact that she stayed at her desk does not cancel them.
answers.text: She did not want to go, and her body showed it even though she never went.

answers.feedback: Her behavior at the door happened before she turned back; that behavior is evidence even though the action never happened.
answers.text: Because she did not go, there is no way to know what she felt.

interaction.question: Mira did not go to the lunch at all. What does her behavior show?

semantic_spec.judgment: 最终没有行动时，负意愿还能被读出来吗？
semantic_spec.observable_signs: door-frame grip, held breath, turned back

experience.episode: Home alone, Tom sees a jar of cookies on the table. No one asked him to eat one, and no one is watching. He walks over, reaches out, his fingers touch the lid, then he pulls his hand back, sighs, and walks away.
observable_evidence: He walks to the jar on his own.
His fingers touch the lid, then pull back.
He sighs after pulling his hand away.
He walks away and does not come back.

surface_dimensions.baseline: someone asks the person to act
surface_dimensions.deviation: nobody asks and nobody watches
surface_dimensions.name: source_of_request

surface_dimensions.baseline: takes the cookie with a smooth reach
surface_dimensions.deviation: touches the lid, then withdraws the hand
surface_dimensions.name: contact

surface_dimensions.deviation: walks away, nothing taken
surface_dimensions.name: outcome

answers.feedback: The action was available and nothing blocked him; his hand touching the lid and pulling back is the readable sign. No outside pressure is needed for this meaning to hold.
answers.text: He did not want to take one even though he easily could have.

answers.feedback: A person can face an available action without any request; the reach-and- withdraw movement still shows how he felt about doing it.
answers.text: Without a request, his behavior shows nothing about what he wanted.

interaction.question: Nobody asked Tom to take a cookie. What does his behavior show?

semantic_spec.judgment: 没有人要求、没有外部压力时，负意愿还成立吗？

experience.episode: In one corner, a boy stands in front of two cupcakes. He looks at the strawberry one, then at the chocolate one, smiles, tilts his head, and happily picks the strawberry one. In the other corner, a girl stands in front of a swing. She steps toward it slowly, her hand touches the chain, then pulls back; she presses her lips together and lets out a small sigh.
observable_evidence: The boy smiles and tilts his head while comparing the two cakes.
The boy picks one cake quickly after looking at both.
The girl steps toward the swing very slowly.
The girl's hand touches the chain, then pulls back.
The girl presses her lips together and sighs.

surface_dimensions.deviation: boy weighs two options (positive case); girl faces one known action (negative case)
surface_dimensions.name: deciding_state

surface_dimensions.deviation: boy's signals are positive; girl's signals are negative
surface_dimensions.name: affective_tone

surface_dimensions.deviation: girl's approach is slow with a pull-back
surface_dimensions.name: approach_behavior

answers.feedback: Her slow approach, the hand that touches and pulls back, and her sigh are negative signs about one known action. The boy is not sure which cake to pick, but his smile and quick pick show a positive attitude, so he is not the one.
answers.text: The girl with the swing.

answers.feedback: He is weighing two options and looks pleased while doing it; being unsure which one to choose is not the same as not wanting to do something.
answers.text: The boy with the cupcakes.

interaction.question: Which child was facing an action he or she could take but did not want to do?

semantic_spec.decision_state: negative case reaches a decision with resistance
semantic_spec.judgment: 积极的犹豫（愿意但不确定）与消极的抵触（不愿意）如何区分？
semantic_spec.willingness_sign: visible in approach and tone, not in the decision

experience.episode: In a quiet office hallway, a manager calls out to Maya about the afternoon report. Maya is walking toward the meeting room. Her steps slow down, she looks down at her phone for a moment, lets out a soft sigh, then pushes the door and walks in.
observable_evidence: Her steps slow down after the call.
She looks down at her phone instead of answering at once.
A soft sigh before she opens the door.
She still pushes the door and walks in.

surface_dimensions.deviation: visibly slows down after the request
surface_dimensions.name: walking_speed

surface_dimensions.deviation: stops to look at her phone for a moment
surface_dimensions.name: attention

surface_dimensions.deviation: goes in the end, with the slow-down still readable
surface_dimensions.name: outcome

answers.feedback: The slowing steps, the pause to look at her phone, and the sigh are negative signs, and they stay readable even though she ended up going.
answers.text: She did not want to go, and the slow-down and sigh showed it while she went anyway.

answers.feedback: Going to the meeting does not erase the signs she gave on the way; her body showed one thing while she still did the action.
answers.text: Because she went, she must have wanted to go.

interaction.question: Maya did go to the meeting. What did her behavior show about how she felt?

semantic_spec.judgment: 换到成年人的工作场合，负意愿还能被读出来吗？
